title: Config-sensitivity snapshotter for JSON field flakiness
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Goal: Build an automated snapshotting and sensitivity-scoring pipeline that links structured-output (JSON) instability to specific config or model changes. This task focuses on detecting 'field flakiness' — fields whose values or types change nondeterministically after deploys or config toggles — and scoring how sensitive each field is to an individual change. The system will produce per-deploy delta heatmaps and ranked hypotheses for root cause (model variant, temperature, quantization profile, prompt template, or new tokenizer).
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline captures end-to-end snapshots of generation outputs for a canonical golden sample set across configured model+config permutations
Generates a field-level flakiness score (0-1) and highlights fields with >0.25 change rate between baseline and candidate
Delta artifacts (heatmaps + sample diffs) are available in Console under Evaluations -> Regression Snapshotter within 24 hours of a gated deploy
Automated hypotheses listing includes top-3 suspected causes (with confidence) and links to the PR that changed the config or model
Smoke tests and e2e harness validate that the snapshotter raises an alert for a synthetic regression injected into the golden set
implementation_plan: Define canonical golden sample set (300 prompts covering typical schema shapes and edge cases) — work with PM and DS
Create lightweight runner that executes each golden prompt across baseline and candidate permutations (model, temp, quant, prompt-tpl) in shadow mode
Canonicalize outputs with tolerant JSON normalization (ordering, whitespace, type coercion rules) before diffing
Compute field-level metrics: presence_change_rate, type_flip_rate, value_entropy_delta, token_length_delta
Aggregate metrics into a sensitivity score using weighted heuristics (weights configurable per project)
Store snapshot artifacts in S3 with index metadata and post results to Console + Slack channel
Add a regression hypothesis generator that correlates config diffs and known change vectors with observed field sensitivity
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer covering maps, arrays, optional fields, and null vs empty distinctions
Synthetic regression test: introduce a prompt-template change that intentionally flips a date format and ensure the snapshotter flags affected fields
A/B shadow run validation against a small set of customer-like prompts to measure false positive rate (target < 5%)
Load test: ensure 300 prompts x 6 permutations completes within 30 minutes on dedicated CI infra
Integration test: Console shows heatmap and linking to PR metadata after a pipeline run
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Alpha): internal-only runs for core models and a handful of configs; collect feedback from Evals and Runtime teams
Phase 2 (Beta): enable for all runtime canaries and surface alerts to oncall; tune weights and thresholds based on false positives
Phase 3 (GA): enable snapshotting on all gated deploys for hosted and dedicated; add customer opt-in for Private deployments
Fallback: if snapshotter run exceeds SLA, mark as deferred and trigger sampling mode that returns partial results
metrics: Field-level sensitivity coverage: percent of schema fields observed in snapshot runs
False positive rate (FP / total alerts) from synthetic validation
Mean time to hypothesis (time from deploy to top-3 hypothesis generation)
Storage cost per snapshot run (S3 size) and runtime cost per prompt
risks: High cardinality schemas could bloat storage and make diffs noisy
Canonicalization choices may hide real regressions (type coercion trade-offs)
Correlation is not causation: hypotheses may point to config changes that co-occur with the true root cause
Snapshot runtime could increase CI costs if not throttled
notes: Decision: use a deterministic canonicalizer with an opt-in strict mode — default is tolerant to ordering and whitespace but not to type changes
Trade-off discussed with Runtime: running full-scale across all permutations gives best signal but costs grow quadratically; we will start with targeted permutations derived from recent deploy diffs
We will reuse existing eval harness infra (ENG-27145 golden diffs) but implement a separate index schema to avoid coupling release cadence
Need to align with Privacy/Security on storing hashed prompt keys for customer-owned prompts
